markdown_report:
The strongest early-stage direction is **candidate-conditioned recent-history attention added to SASRec**, tested as a small residual branch. Its benefits remain hypotheses; the supplied inspiration’s 0.5600 score lacks a matched comparison establishing improvement.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already models temporal dependencies, so another recency mechanism needs an explicit control. (2) User feedback identifies two actionable failures: broad associations crowd out specific matches, and older incidental interactions outweigh recent repeated interests. Candidate-specific evidence selection could address both, without establishing compatibility. (3) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings and a −0.4812 lower-tail margin; modest embedding alignment does not justify prioritizing collapse remedies.

**Insights from related work.** (1) MARS motivates candidate-specific matching of multiple preference signals, but its pretrained text setting exceeds this task’s resources. (2) DARE motivates separate attention and value embeddings; its long-history CTR evidence does not establish transfer here. (3) gSASRec motivates testing sampled-loss calibration before increasing capacity; training-margin improvements still require validation HR@10 confirmation.

The conceptual framework separates **evidence selection** (SASRec attention, candidate attention, interest states), **evidence representation** (ID embeddings or supplied text), and **ranking supervision** (BCE, gBCE, sampled softmax). The selected algorithm changes evidence selection while retaining baseline supervision, making the first experiment easier to interpret.

Scores below are hypotheses. O/P/U/M denote originality, future potential, user-diagnosis alignment, and model-diagnosis alignment; D measures implementation difficulty, with higher meaning harder. Each cell gives one advantage and one limitation.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-negative gBCE [gSASRec] | 2: focused / established | 7: reusable / sampling-sensitive | 3: discriminates / no intent selection | 8: targets confusion / margins insufficient | 3: encoder unchanged / extra sampling |
| Recent candidate attention [MARS, DARE] | 4: useful adaptation / familiar ingredients | 7: extensible / sparse evidence | 8: specificity and recency / no compatibility labels | 7: candidate discrimination / possible overfit | 5: small branch / scorer synchronization |
| Three causal interest states [D2MFRec] | 4: persistent interests / established routing | 7: richer histories / state instability | 7: recurring interests / completion unobserved | 5: differentiated features / indirect margin link | 7: compact states / causal routing complexity |

Select recent candidate attention at 0% progress. Score each candidate using SASRec plus a bounded residual attending to the last ten valid interactions through independent key/query and value embeddings. Recency weights favor current evidence; candidate conditioning lets different candidates retrieve different supporting events. Neither mechanism guarantees semantic precision.

Compare baseline, recency pooling, and candidate attention at matched residual capacity. Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Report existing margin diagnostics and descriptive simulator feedback; claim neither compatibility nor satisfaction gains without evidence.

idea.description: Add a bounded candidate-conditioned attention residual over the ten most recent valid prefix interactions to each dataset’s SASRec model. Use independent embedding tables for attention keys/queries and transition values/targets, retaining the baseline encoder and objective.
idea.motivation: The branch explicitly targets two observed user-facing failures: broad associations displacing specific matches, and old incidental interactions outweighing recent repeated evidence. Candidate-conditioned weights can select supporting history separately for each recommendation, while a fixed recent window and decay constrain old evidence. These are inductive biases, not observed intent or compatibility labels. The model-facing target is weak positive–negative discrimination, especially Electronics’ 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and negative tenth-percentile margin.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the four original datasets and routing, input splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Save every artifact beneath the trial directory and execute on one GPU. Honor SASREC_EPOCHS, default 200. Use no external weights, hidden test data, unavailable metadata, or simulator traits.

Use an ID-only first experiment to isolate evidence selection. Set recent window K=10, branch dimension d=16, decay=0.8, and fixed residual coefficient alpha=0.1 as prespecified engineering choices. Create independent key/query table A, source-value table V, and candidate-target table T, each with padding index zero. Normalize vectors before dot products. For candidate j, attend over valid recent prefix items using cosine(A[item], A[j])/0.2 + lag*log(0.8). The residual is the attention-weighted cosine(V[item], T[j]); its range is bounded. Return zero for empty histories. Mask padding after normalization and exclude padded targets from loss. Initialize all branch tables nonzero; retain baseline loss, optimizer, sampler, and regularization, with explicit reporting of any necessary new parameter groups.

Prespecify three configurations: unchanged SASRec; the same residual with candidate-independent exponential pooling; and candidate attention. The latter two share V/T parameterization; register the same A table in the pooling control for parameter-count parity, noting that unused parameters do not match effective capacity. Preserve baseline initialization and random streams by constructing branches within a forked RNG context after baseline initialization. No additional tuning follows simulator feedback.

Allocate at most 12,000 GPU-seconds per configuration across all four categories, reserving 7,200 seconds for diagnostics, debugging, and failures. Count all work against 43,200 seconds. Use charged baseline timing to freeze a common feasible epoch cap, no greater than the environment limit; compare only checkpoints available at the same completed epoch across every category and configuration. Select by unrounded host macro validation HR@10; prefer baseline on ties. The host retains 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42.

Candidate dependence requires adapting the compatibility view: log2feats returns the encoder features plus sufficient causal recent-item context, while predict_score computes the complete candidate-dependent score. Support aligned B x L targets and B x C candidate lists explicitly. Retain view.model as the actual module, view.item_emb, user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; compute margins using the complete scorer. Label base-table cosine similarity as such, and mark unavailable item-category breakdowns unavailable. Do not interpret dataset names as item-level category metadata.

Update the predictor writer to serialize architecture version, all branch settings and weights, and dataset routing. Reconstruct precisely the same scorer in working/predict.py. Chunk candidates for full-catalog recommendations to the twenty designated training users; normalize attention over history separately for each candidate so chunk size cannot change scores. Verify save/reload equality, causal masking, padding invariance, candidate-order equivariance, and chunked/full scoring agreement using public histories. These checks also consume the search budget. Report measured validation outcomes without claiming that lexical precision, equipment compatibility, or completed needs have been identified.
idea.pseudocode:
class RecentCandidateSASRec(nn.Module):
    def log2feats(sequence):
        h = baseline.log2feats(sequence)
        recent_ids, lags, mask = causal_recent_windows(sequence, K=10)
        return Features(h, recent_ids, lags, mask)

    def score_one_position(features, candidates):
        # candidates: B,C; histories: B,K; all operations stay within user
        base = batched_dot(features.h, item_emb(candidates))
        keys = normalize(A(features.recent_ids))
        queries = normalize(A(candidates))
        logits = einsum('bkd,bcd->bck', keys, queries) / 0.2
        logits += features.lags[:, None, :] * log(0.8)
        weights = safe_masked_softmax(logits, features.mask[:, None, :])
        values = normalize(V(features.recent_ids))
        targets = normalize(T(candidates))
        transition = einsum('bkd,bcd->bck', values, targets)
        residual = sum(weights * transition, axis=-1)
        return base + 0.1 * residual

    def predict_score(features, items):
        # Explicit adapters handle aligned B,L targets or B,C candidates.
        return shape_checked_dispatch(score_one_position, features, items)

for configuration in [baseline, recency_pooling, candidate_attention]:
    for dataset in ORIGINAL_FOUR_DATASETS:
        seed_training(42)
        model = construct_original_sasrec(dataset)
        attach_branch_if_requested_preserving_rng(model, configuration)
        train_with_unchanged_loss_at_common_epoch_cap(model)
        save_configuration_and_state_under_trial_directory(model)
    write_matching_predictor_with_original_dataset_routing()
    record_host_validation_macro_HR10_and_GPU_seconds()
select_highest_host_macro_HR10_with_baseline_tie_preference()
run_compatible_diagnostics_without_additional_tuning()

originality.positive: A constrained adaptation combines candidate-specific evidence selection, independent attention/value tables, and recent causal support around two concrete user failures.
originality.negative: Candidate attention, recency weighting, and additive sequential residuals are established techniques; this is an experimental combination rather than a new model family.

future_potential.positive: Provides a tractable foundation for testing whether candidate-specific support improves ranking, with later extensions using supplied titles and descriptions.
future_potential.negative: Sparse interactions can destabilize attention, and predictive transitions cannot identify compatibility, completed needs, or actual user intent.

code_difficulty.positive: The SASRec encoder and training objective remain intact, and the branch uses small embedding tables with a fixed short window.
code_difficulty.negative: Candidate-dependent training, full-catalog chunking, causal feature packaging, and synchronized predictor and diagnostic implementations require careful handling.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal self-attention to model sequential interaction histories and score next-item candidates.
limitations: Its capabilities already include temporal evidence selection; additional recency mechanisms need controlled comparisons.
Interaction prediction alone does not establish equipment compatibility or consumption completion.

related_work.title: MARS
contributions: Motivates attribute-aware text representations and user–candidate matching across multiple preference signals.
limitations: The supplied summary describes pretrained language representations, which cannot be imported into this task.
Does not establish effectiveness of the proposed ID-only residual.

related_work.title: DARE
contributions: Separates embedding tables used for candidate–history attention and history representation.
Reports interference from sharing those functions in its studied setting.
limitations: Evidence concerns long-history CTR prediction rather than this sparse next-item benchmark.
Separate tables increase parameters and can overfit sparse items.

related_work.title: gSASRec: sampled-loss calibration for sequential recommendation
contributions: Studies overconfidence from sampled BCE and proposes gBCE with increased negative sampling.
limitations: Does not directly select recent candidate-specific evidence.
Its reported improvements do not establish gains under the pinned RecHarness evaluator.

related_work.title: D2MFRec
contributions: Combines soft-clustered interest representations with sequential representations using learned gates.
limitations: Interest differentiation does not establish that inactive interests represent completed needs.
More elaborate interest modeling increases implementation and search costs.
